payload.title: What Are the Baltic Wedding Traditions You Did Not Know?
payload.excerpt: Baltic wedding traditions country by country, from Latvia's midnight mičošana and Lithuania's bread and salt welcome to Estonia's bonnet ceremony, with notes for Australians marrying there or at home.
key_takeaways: Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania each have their own language and customs, so a "Baltic" wedding is really one of three national traditions.
Latvia's mičošana is a midnight ritual, often led by folklore groups, in which the bride symbolically says goodbye to her status as a daughter and takes on the role of wife.
Lithuania marked the same passage with gaubtuvės, the removal of the bride's wreath, and Estonia with tanutamine, when the bride was dressed as a married woman.
As at November 2026 Smartraveller rates all three countries "Exercise normal safety precautions", with "Reconsider your need to travel" for areas of Latvia near the border with Belarus.

faq.a: They are three sets of customs, not one: Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania each have their own language and wedding traditions. Latvia keeps the midnight mičošana, Lithuania the bread and salt welcome, and Estonia recorded the bonnet ceremony, tanutamine.

faq.q: What is mičošana at a Latvian wedding?
faq.a: A midnight ritual, still part of modern Latvian weddings, in which the bride symbolically says goodbye to her status as a daughter and takes on the role of wife. It is often led by folklore groups who sing and perform the ritual.

faq.q: What happens at a traditional Lithuanian wedding?
faq.a: Historically, a matchmaker (piršlys) arranged the match, the families agreed terms, and the betrothal came before the wedding. The couple were welcomed with bread and salt, and the bride's wreath was removed in the gaubtuvės rite.

faq.q: What is the Estonian bonnet ceremony?
faq.a: Tanutamine was the high point of the Estonian wedding, when the bride was dressed in a married woman's bonnet and apron and became a young wife.

faq.q: Are any Baltic wedding customs UNESCO listed?
faq.a: Not as wedding customs on their own. UNESCO's entries for Kihnu (Estonia), the Suiti cultural space (Latvia) and sutartinės (Lithuania) name weddings among their traditions or themes.

faq.q: Can Australians get married in Latvia, Lithuania or Estonia?
faq.a: Yes, but each country has its own process. Ask the local registry whether it needs a CNI and an apostille, then the Australian Embassy in Stockholm (Estonia and Latvia) or Warsaw (Lithuania).
